$comment: Measured tuning profile. Every value below was measured on an idle NVIDIA GB10 and carries its provenance. Nothing here is extrapolated or guessed. Re-generate with: pulse tune

hardware.name: NVIDIA GB10
hardware.provenance: bench_gb10_streaming on an idle GPU; peak is the vendor figure
hardware.bandwidth_provenance: bench/cuda/bw.cu sweeping MLP, block count and occupancy at the model's 6.70 GB working set: 216.9 / 217.6 / 212.4 GB/s over three runs, 79-80% of the 273 GB/s spec peak. At a 4 GB working set the best config reached 229.0 GB/s (84%). An earlier figure of 184.6 GB/s came from a single kernel configuration and under-measured the hardware.
hardware.llama_cpp_decode_efficiency: 183 GB/s achieved = 85% of the 216 GB/s achievable; a 16% software gap

model.provenance: 6.70 GB / 184.6 GB/s. Confirmed: no-drafter batch-1 decode measures 27.54 tok/s = 36.3 ms/token

launch_flags.ubatch_provenance: ubatch 1024 measured worse than 512 on prefill (389 vs 656 tok/s). Do not raise.
launch_flags.batch_provenance: prompts above 2048 tokens fail with the default batch size

parallel_slots.provenance: true batched decode scales 27.54 -> 133.08 tok/s from B=1 to B=16 (llama-batched-bench). llama-server defaults to n_slots=4, which saturates at 73.08 tok/s aggregate with 16 clients; 16 slots reaches 117.71.

v1.note: K=4 (= block_size) beats K=3 on throughput: 63.77 vs 58.08 tok/s. K=3 gives higher acceptance (78.29% vs 72.28%) but fewer tokens per step. Use the full block.

measured.note: cold = first use after CPU activity; warm = sustained serving. Both are real and answer different questions.

v2.correction: an earlier measurement of this exact config reported 73.3 tok/s with a 1.09 spread. That was taken in an unusually favourable machine state. A properly quiesced 6-repeat run gives a 66.31 median with 10.2% spread.

drafters.recommended_provenance: v1 (block 4) at K=4 is the best default: it wins the serving grid at 1, 4 and 8 clients and loses to no-drafter only at 16. v2 (block 7) wins single-stream on code context (71.45 vs ~64) but loses under batching at every level except 2 clients, because batch rows = clients x (K+1) and deeper speculation pushes past mmvq's ncols<=8 into MMQ.

k_policy.rule: never request K above the drafter's block_size
k_policy.provenance: K=5 and K=7 are byte-identical to K=4 with the v1 drafter (4.03 tok/step, 77.52% acceptance, 62.5 ms/step). --spec-draft-n-max past block_size is a no-op.

speculation_by_load.rule: speculate at low concurrency, disable at high concurrency
speculation_by_load.provenance: bench/conc.py against a 16-slot server, 128 tokens per request, temperature 0
speculation_by_load.caveat: llama-server cannot toggle speculation per request: the schema fields speculative.n_max / n_min are compiled out behind '#if 0' in tools/server/server-schema.cpp, and the decode path reads params_base.speculative. Acting on this policy currently requires two backends.

known_negative_results.cuda_graphs: GGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON measured 61.84 vs 62.40 tok/s - no effect. Graphs are disabled at runtime because Gated DeltaNet nodes fail ggml_cuda_graph_check_compability.
known_negative_results.ptq1_0_target: smaller target measured 22% slower (51.73 vs 65.96 tok/s)
known_negative_results.ngram_stacking: counters byte-identical to the drafter alone; never engaged
known_negative_results.batched_lm_head_kernel: no gain available. mul_mat_vec_q already amortises the weight read across ncols_dst; measured +10% kernel time for 2.5x the columns.
known_negative_results.forcing_mmq_earlier: GGML_MMVQ_MAX below 8 measured 34% worse at 5 rows (100.78 -> 75.21)

vs_stock_defaults.$comment: Measured today, idle GB10, same model, same harness (bench/conc.py), 128 tokens/request, temp 0.
vs_stock_defaults.tuned: pulse serve  (16 slots, -fa on, -ub 512, drafter by load policy)

design_curve.$comment: Throughput vs accepted-tokens-per-step at 100% acceptance, measured with a model-free n-gram drafter on repetitive text. This is the hardware ceiling for any drafter, and the spec any drafter must be designed against.
design_curve.method: llama-speculative-simple --spec-type ngram-simple --spec-ngram-simple-size-m M, idle GB10, temp 0
design_curve.base_is_the_weight_sweep: 36.65 ms measured vs 36.3 ms predicted from 6.70 GB / 184.6 GB/s
design_curve.discontinuity_at_8: ncols_dst crosses MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 and dispatch falls from mul_mat_vec_q to MMQ: +14.5 ms for +1.9 tokens. MMQ base ~65 ms, marginal ~1.0 ms/row.
design_curve.threshold_is_correctly_tuned_below_8: forcing MMQ earlier via GGML_MMVQ_MAX measured 34% worse (100.78 -> 75.21 tok/s at 5 rows). Raising it above 8 asserts: mmvq is only template-instantiated to ncols_dst=8, so rows 9-15 are forced onto MMQ although the measured crossover is ~15.

remaining_levers.$comment: Both quantified against the measured design curve. Together they clear 100 tok/s single-stream.

lever_1_drafter_path_overhead.evidence: at 3.86 tok/step the n-gram curve gives 44.9 ms/step; the dspark drafter measures 60.6 ms. Of the 15.7 ms gap only 3.27 ms is the drafter's own 603 MB sweep.

lever_2_deeper_block.evidence: v1 already reaches 90.18% acceptance at depth 3 and 72-78% at depth 3-4

remaining_levers.both: ~100+ tok/s single-stream, no change to the target model

spec_type.provenance: stacking an n-gram drafter helps the shallow v1 drafter (+1.8%: 63.88 -> 65.06) but HURTS the deep v2 drafter (-11%: 73.20 -> 65.28), because free n-gram drafts displace deeper dspark drafts (5.74 -> 4.62 tok/step). With the recommended v2 drafter, do not stack.
spec_type.requires_real_context: an n-gram drafter needs something to look up. On a 60-token prompt it never fires and stacking is a no-op - an earlier round concluded it was broken on exactly that basis.

the_one_remaining_lever.finding: the dspark drafter's forward pass runs at ~39 GB/s, 21% of the 184.6 GB/s this machine achieves
the_one_remaining_lever.method: overhead = measured ms/step minus the n-gram design curve at the same tokens/step. Overhead scales 1.81x for a 1.75x larger drafter, so it is the drafter's forward pass, not a fixed cost.
the_one_remaining_lever.cause: the drafter is a 5-layer block-diffusion model split into ~24 small MMQ launches, none large enough to saturate the bus
the_one_remaining_lever.note: this is a runtime optimization on drafter execution, not a new model. CUDA Graphs will not help: the drafter has Gated DeltaNet layers, which is why graphs are rejected at runtime.
the_one_remaining_lever.caveat: the drafter overhead (27.9 ms of a ~78 ms step, 36%) is well above the 10.2% noise floor, so it is a real target - but it must be validated with the median-of-6 protocol, not single runs.

measurement_protocol.$comment: This machine's throughput is state-dependent. Follow this or you will manufacture fake wins.
measurement_protocol.rule: with 2 warmup runs discarded and configs interleaved, measured spread is 3.4%; without warmup on a cold machine it is 10.2%. Gate claims on 3.4% only if you followed the warm protocol.
measurement_protocol.quiesce: no GPU compute apps, load average below ~1, no heavy CPU processes
measurement_protocol.warmup: throughput climbs across consecutive runs (63.4 -> 62.4 -> 64.6 -> 68.1 -> 69.2 -> 68.0). Unified-memory pages migrate back to the GPU lazily. Discard the first runs.
measurement_protocol.cpu_bus_contention: GB10 shares one LPDDR5X bus between CPU and GPU. 8 CPU threads streaming memory cost 16% of decode throughput (73.3 -> 61.0), and throughput did not recover immediately when the load stopped.
measurement_protocol.do_not_use_nsys: CUPTI under-reports kernel duration on GB10 unified memory: it showed 2.7 ms of kernel work inside a 73.4 ms step, and 92% GPU idle on a workload two independent processes proved bandwidth-saturated. Use wall-clock differentials.

cold_vs_warm.$comment: Identical config, identical command, three protocols.

n6_quiesced_no_warmup.note: cold start; runs climb as pages migrate back

n4_warmup2_interleaved.note: warm steady state; the sustained-serving number

serving_policy.$comment: Measured 2D grid: drafter x concurrent clients, bench/grid.sh, 16 slots, 128 tok/request. Batch rows = clients x (K+1), so deeper speculation multiplies under batching and crosses mmvq's ncols<=8 limit into MMQ's high-fixed-cost regime (see Round 8 discontinuity).

rule.note: v2 (block 7) is only worth it for SINGLE-STREAM on high-acceptance workloads such as code, where it measured 71.45 vs v1's ~64. Under batching it loses at every level except 2 clients.

serving_policy.caveat: the grid used short chat-style prompts and saw 29-43% acceptance; the single-stream code-context tests saw 69-72%. Acceptance is workload-dependent (measured range 21%-96%), so the optimal drafter depends on prompt type as well as concurrency.

context_model.$comment: Validated decode-throughput model vs context length. Measured with llama-batched-bench in a SINGLE process (model resident) so cold-start cannot confound it.
context_model.kv_geometry: 16 attention layers (every 4th of 64, hybrid) x 4 kv heads x (key 256 + value 256) x 2 bytes

efficiency.note: drifts down at extreme context; use ~0.80 beyond 128k

context_model.below_16k_does_not_resolve: rows at 128-4096 swing 2.1x non-monotonically (26.37, 19.08, 17.40, 12.40, 14.04) because KV is under 16% of the step and noise exceeds the effect. Do not read a context trend there.

prefill.note: cold prefill at 131072 takes 211.7 s, roughly 7 minutes at 256k. Prompt/prefix caching dominates long-context UX far more than decode speed. Unmeasured here.

projection_256k.conclusion: drafter alone does not reliably clear 50-70 tok/s at 256k; KV compression is required

kv_quantization.$comment: Measured at 64k context with llama-batched-bench. KV compression delivers ~43% of its theoretical bandwidth benefit here; the rest is lost to dequantization.

recommendation_by_context.why: KV is under 16% of the step; q8_0 measured slightly WORSE than f16 at short context
KV exceeds the model size; this is the dominant term

q4_0.note: clears the 50-70 target with the drafter we already have

projection_256k.caveat: at 50% acceptance (what the drafter currently degrades to by 4k) q4_0 gives 47 tok/s and misses the target. Both levers are needed.

kv_quantization.quality_caveat: these are throughput measurements only. q4_0 KV carries an accuracy cost that has NOT been measured here. TurboQuant's contribution is better distortion at low bit-width, which is exactly what a naive q4_0 does not give you.

cache_reuse_unavailable.status: silently disabled at load on this model
cache_reuse_unavailable.reason: server-context.cpp:1132 gates it on llama_memory_can_shift(); llama-kv-cache.cpp:1176 returns false when hparams.n_pos_per_embd() > 1. Bonsai 2 uses mRoPE (rope.dimension_sections = [11,11,10]), so K-shift is refused. This is mRoPE, NOT the Gated DeltaNet hybrid - recurrent memory reports shifting as trivially supported.
cache_reuse_unavailable.consequence: any edit before the tail costs a full re-prefill: 242 ms vs ~8700 ms at 8k, a 36x cliff

prefix_caching.cache_ram_warning: KV at 256k is 17 GB, more than double the default prompt-cache budget. Raise --cache-ram for long-context deployments.
